summary: I rebuilt the light curve vet-v3 saw and measured every epoch to test the three kills (odd_even, sector_depth, holdout) against partial coverage, TTVs, low SNR, dilution and one-sector artefacts. All three stand at 34.94 d, and all three rest on one fact: both odd epochs with data (11 in S27, 41 in S66) are flat at full coverage, while every even epoch with usable data (0, 42, 62, and 72 in the timing-suspect S104) shows a 6-hour dip within 0.3 h of a linear ephemeris. The dips look like a 69.878-day signal, twice the search's period and past its 40-day cap, at which vet-v3's five light-curve checks pass; that is the one hold.

findings.claim: The odd_even kill stands at 34.94 d: both odd transits with data are flat at full coverage, so it is not a partly covered transit, a TTV, low SNR or a dilution change.
findings.evidence: checks.json odd_even pdcsap: odd -117 +- 133 ppm (n 34) vs even 841 +- 101 (n 144), 5.7 sigma. Per epoch (/tmp/t13/410399327-1/scan.out, from /tmp/t13/heavy.sh bash -c 'cd ~/code/tess-hunt && uv run python /tmp/t13/410399327-1/scan.py ~/.cache/tess-hunt/drafts/m3/410399327-1/checks.json ~/.cache/tess-hunt/drafts/m3/410399327-1/checks-with-suspect.json'; plot /tmp/t13/410399327-1/epochs.png): epoch 11 (S27) core -156 +- 149 ppm on 18 of 18 core cadences, raw data -36 h to +36 h; epoch 41 (S66) 41 +- 298 on 16 of 54 core cadences because TOI-7925.01's mask cuts the rest (its transit falls 1.52 h after our mid, mask +-2.12 h), and 97 +- 164 on all 54 with the mask off and +-0.3 d held out of the trend. A 6-h box slid +-12 h around each odd epoch finds nothing above 2.3 sigma (epoch 11: +6.3 h, 198 +- 106 ppm, where TOI-7925.01's own transit falls at +4.31 h; epoch 41: +3.3 h, 266 +- 116), so no TTV-shifted transit hides nearby, and the even dips sit within 0.3 h of the linear ephemeris (epoch 0 +0.3 h, 42 0.0 h, 62 -0.3 h, 72 -0.3 h). Not low SNR: the expected depth is 0.75 to 0.84 ppt against errors of 0.15 to 0.16 ppt (holdout season 1 expected SNR 4.9). Not dilution: CROWDSAP S27 0.977, S66 0.974, S67 0.976 (checks.json sources); S66 and S67 are consecutive TESS-SPOC sectors with the same crowding, yet epoch 41 is flat and epoch 42, one period later, is 1106 +- 140 ppm. QLP's odd_even pass rests on its one odd transit, epoch 63, which is a sector-end ramp (F5). Empty odd epochs are what a period of twice 34.94 d gives, not a binary's alternating depths (F4).

findings.claim: The sector_depth kill stands at 34.94 d: the chi-square comes from S27's empty odd epoch and S67's deep even one, not from the partly covered S66 transit or dilution.
findings.evidence: checks.json sector_depth pdcsap: S13 551 +- 146, S27 -156 +- 149 (n 18), S66 41 +- 298 (n 16), S67 1106 +- 140 ppm; chi2 40.7, dof 3, p 7.5e-09. Chi-square terms (/tmp/t13/410399327-1/twice.out, from /tmp/t13/heavy.sh bash -c 'cd ~/code/tess-hunt && uv run python /tmp/t13/410399327-1/twice.py ~/.cache/tess-hunt/drafts/m3/410399327-1/checks.json ~/.cache/tess-hunt/drafts/m3/410399327-1/checks-with-suspect.json'): S13 0.16, S27 18.93, S66 2.29, S67 19.33. Without the partly covered S66: chi2 38.25, dof 2, p 4.95e-09, still a fail. Without S27: p 9.1e-04, still a fail. Without S27 and S66: p 5.9e-03, a pass. So the fail needs S27, a fully covered epoch with no dip (F1). PDCSAP is crowding-corrected and CROWDSAP runs 0.974 to 0.991 over S13, S27, S66 and S67, so a dilution change of 2% cannot take 0.8 ppt to -0.16 ppt. QLP is compared only with itself and passes (p 0.72) on S93 and S94, S94 being the ramp of F5.

findings.claim: The holdout kill stands on season 1 (S27); season 0's miss is the refit ephemeris drifting 5.2 hours, not a missing transit.
findings.evidence: checks.json holdout season 1: predicted P 34.93872, t0 1666.7528, so epoch 11 at BTJD 2051.079 (the search's own epoch-11 time is 2051.080); depth -150 +- 153 ppm against an expected 753, tension 5.0, expected SNR 4.9, with S27 fully covered (F1). Season 0: the refit without S13 gives P 34.935329, t0 2051.2559, which puts epoch 0 at BTJD 1666.9673, 5.19 h after the search t0 (/tmp/t13/410399327-1/twice.out); with the refit's 0.1875 d duration the core window spans +4.1 h to +6.3 h, after the dip's egress. The dip is there: the best 6-h box sits +0.3 h from the search t0 at 936 +- 103 ppm (scan.out), and checks.json gives S13 551 +- 146 at the search ephemeris. The drift comes from extrapolating 42 cycles back from training dips at epochs 42 and 62 alone (the refit puts epoch 42 1.52 h late) and stays without S94 (+5.23 h), so it is not the S94 ramp. Not TTVs: the even dips sit within 0.3 h of a linear ephemeris. The fail therefore rests on season 1 alone, the same empty odd epoch as F1 and F2.

findings.claim: The three kills show that 34.94 d is the wrong period, not that the dips are no planet: every usable dip falls on an even epoch, consistent with a 69.878-d transit that the search's 40-d cap could not find and that no check has vetted, and at that period vet-v3's five light-curve checks pass.
findings.evidence: Dips at epochs 0 (S13), 42 (S67), 62 (S93) and 72 (S104, timing-suspect; 0022 puts QLP's offsets under 36 min, small against a 6-h transit): best 6-h boxes within 0.3 h of the linear ephemeris at 936 +- 103, 1194 +- 98, 1063 +- 117 and 1002 +- 125 ppm (/tmp/t13/410399327-1/scan.out). Odd epochs 11 and 41 are flat (F1), odd epoch 63 is a ramp (F5), and epoch 70 has no core data (cut at a gap edge). Shorter periods the even epochs also allow fail: at 2P/3 (23.29 d) the one extra window reads 139 +- 149 ppm, at 2P/5 (13.98 d) the eight extra windows read 19 +- 59 (/tmp/t13/410399327-1/aliases.out, from /tmp/t13/heavy.sh bash -c 'cd ~/code/tess-hunt && uv run python /tmp/t13/410399327-1/aliases.py ~/.cache/tess-hunt/drafts/m3/410399327-1/checks.json ~/.cache/tess-hunt/drafts/m3/410399327-1/checks-with-suspect.json'). vet-v3's own check functions at P = 69.877932 d on the light curve vet-v3 saw (/tmp/t13/410399327-1/twice.out): odd_even pass at 2.8 sigma (S13 551 +- 146 vs S67 1106 +- 140, close to the 3.0 line), secondary pass (+1.4 sigma, 111 +- 81 ppm over the odd epochs), sector_depth pass (p 0.006), holdout pass (2 seasons predicted, season 0 at 575 +- 148), signal_present 9.9 sigma; with the suspect sectors in, all pass, holdout on 3 seasons, 10.6 sigma. Density: the flat fit's log rho -0.227 (+0.167) rises by log10(2) at twice the period (rho scales with P at a fixed transit shape), to 0.074 (1.19 g/cm3) against the TIC's 0.340 +- 0.091: 1.40 sigma instead of 2.98. Radius roughly 2.5 Earth radii (2.09 x sqrt(841/599), even-epoch core depth over the combined one, checks.json). criteria/search-v2.toml [search] period_max_days = 40.0. Triage's two good-quality centroids are on sectors with even-epoch dips: S93 3.3" (quality 0.75) and S104 3.2" (0.69). Untested at 69.88 d: the shape, density and radius fits, ModShift (it ran at 34.94 d: 4.09 sigma at phase 0.591), TRICERATOPS (it did not judge this signal) and the neighbours (Gaia DR3 6434209314080910208 at 19.6" needs a 52% eclipse). What would decide: the maintainer's call, with a decision record, on vetting these dips at 69.878 d, since the search cannot propose that period; then S114's transit at BTJD 4461.87 (epoch 80, even, predicted at both periods; the dossier's window is 4461.847 +- 47.6 min) with 2-min data for the shape.

refuters.reason:
F4 reproduces. I reran all three of the reviewer's scripts and got byte-identical output, and every other number in the finding matches its run file.

Command: copies of scan.py, aliases.py and twice.py in /tmp/t13/410399327-1/refute-F4-reproduce/. The only edit was scan.py's savefig path. twice.py and aliases.py diff identical to the originals. All three ran through `/tmp/t13/heavy.sh bash -c "cd ~/code/tess-hunt && uv run python $D/<script>.py $C/checks.json $C/checks-with-suspect.json > $D/<script>.out"` (C = ~/.cache/tess-hunt/drafts/m3/410399327-1), exit 0. `diff` against /tmp/t13/410399327-1/{twice,scan,aliases}.out: identical for all three.

1. **The light curve is vet-v3's.** twice.py's first block (the search ephemeris) matches checks.json to the ppm: odd_even pdcsap -117+-133 (n 34) vs 841+-101 (n 144), 5.7 sigma; the sector depths; p 7.5e-09; holdout seasons 0 and 1 missed at tensions 7.62 and 5.00. twice.py's thresholds (3.0, 0.001, 7.0, min_points 5) match criteria/vet-v3.toml. It calls the checks the same way src/tess_hunt/vet.py lines 179-245 does (good_timestamps, detrend with the masks, red_noise_beta at core times duration, per_family split).

2. **At P = 69.877932 d** the reproduced output gives:
   - odd_even pass, 2.8 sigma (1106+-140 vs 551+-146)
   - secondary pass, +1.4 sigma (111+-81 ppm, n 161)
   - sector_depth p 0.00594, above min_p_value 0.001
   - holdout pass: 2 seasons predicted, season 0 at 575+-148
   - signal_present 9.9 sigma
   - suspect sectors in: all pass, 3 holdout seasons predicted, 10.6 sigma

3. **Epochs and aliases.** Best 6-h boxes: epoch 0 +0.3 h, 936+-103; epoch 42 0.0 h, 1194+-98; epoch 62 -0.3 h, 1063+-117; epoch 72 -0.3 h, 1002+-125 ppm. Epoch 70 has n 0 core cadences. Aliases: 2P/3 extra window 139+-149 ppm; 2P/5 eight extra windows 19+-59 ppm.

4. **Density, checks.json.** fit_log_rho -0.22705, plus 0.16720; tic_log_rho 0.34035, sd 0.09139; tension 2.978. physical.py line 64 computes tension as abs(mid - log_tic)/hypot(err_fit, err_tic). Recomputed with log10(2) added: 0.074, 1.186 g/cm3, 1.398 sigma.

5. **Radius.** 2.0864 x sqrt(841/598.74) = 2.47.

6. **Other values in checks.json.**
   - ModShift sig_sec 4.089 at phs_sec 0.5908.
   - Pixels: S93 3.31" (quality 0.749), S104 3.24" (0.692), S94 27.08" (0.159).
   - windows: epoch 80, sector 114, mid 4461.8474, sd 47.65 min. Search t0 + 80P = 4461.8684.

7. **Citations and other files.**
   - criteria/search-v2.toml [search] has period_max_days = 40.0.
   - neighbours.csv: 6434209314080910208 at sep 19.589", required_depth 0.5217, possible True. Recomputed from the DR3 positions: 19.59".
   - Decision 0022, lines 12-13: single transits in reliable pairs at up to +35.25 min.
   - dossier.md line 36: TRICERATOPS "did not judge this signal".

No number the finding rests on fails to reproduce.

The kill stands under the rules. F4 does not show it is wrong. It proposes a different signal, and its hold rating does not fit the short brief.

1. The checks worked as designed. docs/design.md 5.2 gives odd/even's planted failure as "Eclipsing binary at twice the period" and the held-out season's as "Wrong period". F4's own account, every dip on an even epoch with the true period at twice 34.94 d, is exactly that case. F1 to F3, from the same reviewer, find no bug, no misread artefact and none of 0031's causes behind the three fails: partial coverage, TTVs, low SNR and dilution are all ruled out. 0031 handles its nearest control the same way. For TOI-396.01, a linear ephemeris that can't fold the planet, it says "the checks did what they are built to do" and keeps "a fail on any of these checks still kills a candidate (decision 0028)". Decision 0028 and M3 design 4.9 define the outcomes: killed means a check failed, and held means "not passed and not killed".

2. The rating does not fit the brief. The short brief rates hold "when the kill looks wrong". F4 accepts the kills at 34.94 d and asks to vet a 69.878-d signal instead. The frozen search cannot produce that period (criteria/search-v2.toml [search] period_max_days = 40.0; docs/design.md 4.1 "BLS ... 1-40 d"), and M3 design section 5 says "No change to the search". The first thing F4 says would decide it is "the maintainer's call, with a decision record". That is a process step, not public data the case is waiting on, so it misses the brief's hold definition: "the public data can't decide". Shape, density, radius, ModShift and neighbours at 69.88 d can all be run on data already in hand. A 2-min transit already exists: checks.json sources list S13 as SPOC, cadence_s 120.0. Under 0028 a confirmed hold reaches the maintainer as a recommended hold on 410399327-1, a signal whose three failed checks the review itself confirms. This belongs in a note, which goes to the maintainer's eye and decides nothing.

3. The evidence is overstated. "vet-v3's five light-curve checks pass" counts one comparison twice. At 69.88 d, odd_even and sector_depth both rest on the single PDCSAP pair S13 551 +- 146 vs S67 1106 +- 140. In QLP, odd_even is inconclusive and sector_depth has only S93, which cannot be tested (/tmp/t13/410399327-1/twice.out). Running python3 on those numbers (/tmp/t13/410399327-1/refute-F4-rules/calc.out) gives z = 2.744 and chi2 = 7.53 on 1 dof, p = 0.0061. That is the reviewer's sector_depth p of 0.0059 to rounding. So the two passes are one statistic, 0.26 sigma from the 3.0 line (vet-v3.toml [odd_even] max_sigma = 3.0). The holdout's two predicted seasons pass at tensions of 2.85 and 2.69 against [holdout] max_depth_tension = 3.0 (twice.out). The maintainer should still see the 69.878-d possibility as a note, or as a proposal for a decision record. As a hold on this signal, it misreads 0028's outcomes and the brief's definition of hold.

findings.claim: The one odd-epoch dip, epoch 63 in QLP S94, sits on a steep sector-end ramp, so QLP's odd_even and sector_depth passes at 34.94 d don't support that period.
findings.evidence: Raw S94 flux, normalized to the sector median (/tmp/t13/410399327-1/twice.out): -3848 ppm 2.25 to 2.0 d before the last cadence (BTJD 3868.503), -6528 ppm 1.0 to 0.75 d before, -15054 ppm in the last 6 h, steepening throughout. Epoch 63's mid (3867.906) is 14.3 h before the end, 2.3 h before the detrend's 0.5-d edge cut (criteria/search-v2.toml edge_cutoff_days), and its depth moves from 803 +- 189 ppm to 1616 +- 187 ppm depending only on how the trend is fitted (scan.out). Triage's S94 centroid (27.1", quality 0.16) measures this ramp. Epoch 70 in S101 sits on a similar ramp before a gap at BTJD 4112.92. See /tmp/t13/410399327-1/epochs.png.

findings.claim: ExoFOP's TOI-7925.01 note already names two of these dips, epochs 42 and 62, as possible unrelated transits, without a period.
findings.evidence: literature.json search.exofop.tois: TOI 7925.01 (2.607 d, PC, source qlp-s93-ffi, TOI date 2026-08-27) notes "potential deeper unrelated transits near TBJD 3134 and 3833"; our epochs 42 and 62 fall at BTJD 3134.188 and 3832.967. CTOIs on the star: none. No TOI, CTOI or paper gives these dips a period, so a 69.878-d signal would be new, but a CTOI should credit the note.

findings.claim: The literature hit 2018A&A...609A.116R (a Gaia red clump calibration) doesn't make the star a giant: Gaia DR3 puts it on the main sequence.
findings.evidence: checks.json star: TIC radius 0.872 solar radii, Gaia DR3 FLAME radius 0.884, logg_flame 4.548, logg_gspphot 4.543, RUWE 1.03. The other four hits (2013AJ....146..134K, 2017AJ....153...75K, 2020AJ....160...83S, 2014AJ....148...81M) are RAVE data releases and APASS photometry of RAVE stars; the star is a RAVE target (SIMBAD name RAVE J192459.5-660924). None names it as a planet host, a binary, a variable or a multiple.
